content:
Apple has finally responded to soaring memory and component costs—and it isn't pulling any punches. Some products are seeing price hikes of over 50%, while memory and storage upgrades are doubling in cost.

Those price hikes are likely here to stay for years—and possibly forever…

9to5Mac readers have long questioned whether Apple will ever reverse course, even as component shortages ease. More than two-thirds of you expect the hikes to be permanent.

Analyst reports have since suggested that supply chain pricing won't improve before 2028, and even then, only marginally. Today's elevated prices are likely to persist for at least several years—and possibly never return to previous levels.

So if this turns out to be true, how are you handling it? Are you gritting your teeth and continuing to buy Apple products at the same pace? Cutting back on how many or how often you buy? Or taking other steps, like choosing cheaper models, buying refurbished, or waiting for sales?

Take our poll and share your thoughts in the comments. There are multiple options so you can express more than one planned change to your buying habits.
